headline: SILVER CRASHES 7%: Hot CPI Kills Rate-Cut Hopes — Metals Selloff Erases Week of Gains
snippet: April CPI printed 3.8% year-over-year — the hottest since May 2023 — triggering a synchronized selloff that sent silver down 6.5%+ from $88 to $77.52 and gold down 2% to $4,564. The gold/silver ratio widened to 58.9:1 from 53.6:1 in a single session as the 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 4.544%, its highest in nearly a year.

headline: AGNICO EAGLE BETS C$14 BILLION ON ONTARIO GOLD — Detour Lake Underground Could Hit 1Moz/yr by 2054
snippet: Agnico Eagle Mines committed C$14 billion ($10.2B USD) to Ontario gold mining through 2030, anchored by a potential Detour Lake Underground expansion that could push Canada's largest open-pit mine past 1 million oz/yr through 2054. The Upper Beaver project near Kirkland Lake would add 210,000 oz Au and 3,600 tonnes Cu annually. Ontario responded by announcing faster permit approvals for mining projects.

headline: BRAZIL VMS DISCOVERY: Meridian Mining Opens Álamo Zone + Hits 10.7m @ 76.7g/t Ag at Cabaçal
snippet: Meridian Mining (TSX: MNO) announced the Álamo gold-silver-copper-zinc discovery at its Cabaçal VMS belt in Brazil, 1km from Santa Helena's infrastructure, while also reporting high-grade results at Santa Helena Central including 10.7m @ 2.5g/t Au, 2.4% Cu, 76.7g/t Ag and 11.7% Zn from 73m. The Álamo zone lies along a 1.6km IP anomaly and is open in all directions.

headline: THE GOLD PARADOX EXPLAINED: Why 3.8% CPI Made Gold Fall, Not Rise
snippet: When CPI beats consensus, rate-cut odds collapse, the dollar strengthens, and gold — priced in dollars — falls in nominal terms despite inflation being the metal's long-run ally. GoldSilver.com dissects the counterintuitive mechanism and explains why today's sharp selloff doesn't invalidate the structural bull case for precious metals.

headline: GDX -6.2%, GDXJ -6.5%: Analysts Call Today's Mining Stock Crash a Healthy Flush, Not a Reversal
snippet: Gold and silver mining ETFs fell more than 6% on May 15 after April CPI hit 3.8%, with Silvercorp (-6.9%), Teck Resources (-5.9%), and Endeavour Silver (-4.9%) among the hardest hit. Leading analysts note that GDX sat over 40% above its 200-day moving average before the selloff — calling the flush a corrective reset within the ongoing bull market, not a structural reversal.

headline: LITHIUM SURGES 23% IN A MONTH: Zimbabwe Export Squeeze and AI Data Centres Drive China to 3-Year High
snippet: Battery-grade lithium carbonate in China rose 23.3% month-on-month to ~CNY 175,000/tonne — the highest in nearly three years — as Zimbabwe's export quotas tightened roughly 7% of global supply and AI data centre operators emerged as an unexpected demand driver alongside EV manufacturers. The price is up 197% year-over-year.

headline: MP MATERIALS OR LYNAS? Motley Fool Names Its Top Rare Earth Stock to Hold for the Next Decade
snippet: With the U.S. DoD backing MP Materials with a $400M equity stake and a 10-year NdPr offtake agreement, and $1.6B in federal funding committed to USA Rare Earth, the western rare earth supply chain is finally getting capitalized. Motley Fool assesses which producer holds the strongest structural advantage as NdPr oxide consolidates near $99/kg — still 88% above January's open.

headline: WHY ANALYSTS STILL SEE $5,000 GOLD — JPMorgan, TD Securities Hold Targets Despite Selloff
snippet: Gold hit an all-time high of $5,589 on January 28 before pulling back to $4,694 by May 12. Despite today's CPI-driven drop, JPMorgan forecasts a Q4 2026 average of $5,055 and TD Securities projects highs near $5,400. Central banks bought a net 244 tonnes in Q1 alone — GoldSilver.com argues the structural demand case is unchanged.
